newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada apologizes for alleging Airbus kickbacks.
newsitem.headline: Canada apologizes for alleging Airbus kickbacks.

text.p: The federal government, building on an apology it was forced to give to former Prime Minister Brian Mulroney, told two other men on Thursday it was sorry it had called them criminals in an alleged Airbus bribery deal.

The government had written the Swiss authorities asking for judicial assistance in investigating Mulroney as well as former Conservative provincial premier Frank Moores and businessman Karlheinz Schreiber.
The investigation concerned alleged kickbacks in Air Canada's $1.8 billion Canadian ($1.3 billion) purchase of Airbus jets in 1988.

"Some of the language contained in the Request for Assistance indicates, wrongly, that the RCMP (Royal Canadian Mounted Police) had reached conclusions that you had engaged in criminal activity," the government wrote the men.
"The Government of Canada and the RCMP fully apologize to you for that language, and regret any effect it may have had on you or your family."
The letter, sent individually to the two men, was signed by Justice Minister Allan Rock and RCMP Commissioner Philip Murray.

On Sunday, on the eve of the opening of a $50 million Canadian ($37 million) libel suit against the government by Mulroney, an out-of-court settlement was reached providing for an apology to Mulroney and payment of his legal bills.
But the settlement made no mention of the two other men for which the government had also sought banking information.
All three denied any wrongdoing, and Mulroney pointed out that the government apology stated that based on evidence to date any conclusion of wrongdoing was unjustified.

The 1995 request for Swiss assistance stated there was criminal activity rather than the Mounties were investigating possible criminal activity. But the letters of apology said this was standard language at the time.
Canada's Liberal government, which trounced the Conservatives in 1993 elections, has been under heavy opposition and media criticism this week over its handling of the Airbus affair.
